sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()
 * \brief Queue a request to the device
 * \param[in] camera The camera to queue the request to
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the device for processing. The
 * request contains a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of
 * parameters. The pipeline handler shall program the device to ensure that the
 * parameters will be applied to the frames captured in the buffers provided in
 * the request.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

original_finding.claim_quote: Implementers of queueRequestDevice must, when processing a request that contains a buffer set and a parameter set connected to a stream, configure the device so that the parameters apply to the frames captured into the buffers provided in the request. Implementers of queueRequestDevice must return 0 on success and a negative error code on failure. PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice() is called from the CameraManager thread.

cases.current_en: Camera::queueRequest() is marked as thread-safe and, before accepting a capture request, calls d->isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning) to check that the camera is in the Running state. When allowDisconnected is false and disconnected_ is true, isAccessAllowed() returns -ENODEV before comparing states. After the connection check passes, if the current state differs from the required state, the returned value is -EACCES, and queueRequest() returns that value unchanged. When both conditions apply, -ENODEV, which indicates a disconnection, takes precedence over -EACCES, and callers must call queueRequest() only when the camera is in the Running state.

request-controls-contract.text:
* \fn Request::controls()
 * \brief Retrieve the request's ControlList
 *
 * Requests store a list of controls to be applied to all frames captured for
 * the request. They are created with an empty list of controls that can be
 * accessed through this function. Control values can be retrieved using
 * ControlList::get() and updated using ControlList::set().
 *
 * Only controls supported by the camera to which this request will be
 * submitted shall be included in the controls list. Attempting to add an
 * unsupported control causes undefined behaviour.
 *
 * \return A reference to the ControlList in this request
 */

request-buffers-contract.text:
* \fn Request::buffers()
 * \brief Retrieve the request's streams to buffers map
 *
 * Return a reference to the map that associates each Stream part of the
 * request to the FrameBuffer the Stream output should be directed to.
 *
 * \return The map of Stream to FrameBuffer
 */
